assessment.scope: Project-owned localhost containers and fictional accounts

tests.expected: Alice receives HTTP 403 for Bob's ticket
Normal user receives HTTP 403 for the administrator route
Administrator can access the administrator route
tests.evidence: GET /Admin using the fictional administrator session

tests.expected: POST without anti-forgery token is rejected
Unknown ticket identifier returns HTTP 404 without a stack trace
tests.evidence: GET a non-existent all-zero ticket identifier
Uploaded payload.exe to Alice's fictional ticket

tests.expected: File larger than 2 MB is rejected
tests.evidence: Uploaded a local generated file larger than the application limit

tests.expected: Path components are removed from the original filename
tests.evidence: Uploaded a fictional filename containing ../ path components

tests.expected: File content is verified against the declared type
tests.evidence: Uploaded HTML bytes with .pdf extension and application/pdf declaration

tests.expected: Required browser security headers are present
Repeated login attempts eventually receive HTTP 429
tests.evidence: Low-volume repeated login requests using nonexistent fictional identities

findings.title: Upload validation trusts the declared file type
findings.evidence: Test A04-SIGNATURE accepted HTML bytes as invoice.pdf when the extension and client-declared Content-Type matched the allowlist.
findings.reproduction: Upload non-PDF bytes using filename invoice.pdf and Content-Type application/pdf to an owned fictional ticket.
findings.cause: The validator checks extension, length and the client-declared MIME value, but does not inspect a file signature or parsed content.
findings.impact: A crafted file can be stored and served under a trusted-looking type, increasing content-confusion and downstream processing risk.
findings.recommendation: Validate magic bytes or parse supported formats server-side; store the detected type and reject mismatches.

findings.title: Uploaded files are not quarantined or malware-scanned
findings.evidence: Static review found no quarantine state, antivirus integration or asynchronous malware scan before attachments become downloadable.
findings.reproduction: Review TicketsController, FileUploadValidator and application service registrations for a scanning or quarantine workflow.
findings.cause: Accepted files are written directly to the application upload volume and immediately exposed through the authorised download action.
findings.impact: An authorised user could store malicious content that later reaches another authorised user or downstream tool.
findings.recommendation: Add a quarantine state, malware scanning service, scan result audit event and release files only after a clean result.

findings.title: Login rate limiting uses a shared global bucket
findings.evidence: Program.cs registers one AddFixedWindowLimiter policy without partitioning by source address or account identifier. Test A01 confirmed the shared policy reaches HTTP 429.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the login rate-limiter registration and send a small number of login requests from separate fictional sessions.
findings.cause: The fixed window is global to the named policy rather than partitioned per source or account.
findings.impact: One client can consume the allowance and temporarily affect unrelated users, while distributed abuse is not separated by source.
findings.recommendation: Use AddPolicy with RateLimitPartition keyed by a privacy-conscious source/account composite and retain a bounded global backstop.

findings.title: Content Security Policy permits inline styles
findings.reproduction: Inspect the Content-Security-Policy response header returned by GET /.
findings.cause: Inline styles are permitted rather than being restricted with hashes, nonces or external stylesheets only.
findings.impact: The policy provides weaker protection against style-based injection and makes future CSP hardening more difficult.
findings.recommendation: Remove unsafe-inline by moving styles to static files or authorising only required styles through hashes/nonces.

findings.title: Application container root filesystem is writable
findings.evidence: compose.yml does not set read_only: true for the application container.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the app service configuration and Docker runtime ReadonlyRootfs value.
findings.cause: The application container can write outside its dedicated upload volume.
findings.impact: A compromised process has a larger writable surface for staging files or modifying runtime state.
findings.recommendation: Enable a read-only root filesystem and add explicit writable tmpfs/volume mounts only where required.

findings.title: Container runtime privileges are not explicitly reduced
findings.evidence: compose.yml does not both drop all Linux capabilities and enable no-new-privileges.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the app service CapDrop and SecurityOpt runtime values.
findings.cause: The container relies on Docker defaults rather than an explicit least-privilege runtime policy.
findings.impact: If application code is compromised, unnecessary kernel capabilities or privilege transitions can increase impact.
findings.recommendation: Set cap_drop: [ALL], security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true], and add back only a demonstrated required capability.

findings.title: Container base images are referenced by mutable tags
findings.owasp: OWASP A08:2021 – Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.evidence: Dockerfile FROM instructions are not pinned to registry digests: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine AS build; FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine AS final
findings.reproduction: Inspect every FROM instruction in infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile.
findings.cause: Version tags can be repointed and do not uniquely identify the bytes used for a build.
findings.impact: A future rebuild can consume different base-image content without a source change, weakening reproducibility and provenance.
findings.recommendation: Pin each base image by verified digest and update the digest through a reviewed dependency PR.

findings.title: Upload request size is not limited before model binding
findings.evidence: The application checks IFormFile.Length in FileUploadValidator but configures no endpoint or form multipart limit near the 2 MB business rule.
findings.reproduction: Inspect upload endpoint attributes and FormOptions/Kestrel request-limit configuration.
findings.cause: The framework can accept and buffer a request substantially larger than the business limit before controller validation rejects it.
findings.impact: Repeated oversized requests can consume more memory, disk or connection time than intended.
findings.recommendation: Set an endpoint RequestSizeLimit and MultipartBodyLengthLimit close to the allowed file size, with a small multipart overhead allowance.
